what_happened: The job asked for commit records from the landing queue after each landing, plus confirming the append-only conflict rule (build job 8). It was rejected at the final verdict with two major findings and no listed unmet criteria or failed checks. First, the behaviour was built only as a hook. The default hook in drain.rs:633 has no real override, so no records are committed from the landing queue and record ordering is unchanged. Second, the second half of build job 8, confirming the append-only conflict rule, was explicitly left undone (async-drain.md:241).
cause: The acceptance criteria were met by showing that a hook and a doc entry exist, not that the landing queue commits real records after each landing. Nothing required a test that runs a real landing and checks that the record commit happened. Nothing tied each half of a two-part build item to its own criterion, so the producer could skip the conflict-rule half and note it as left undone. Only the final verifier compares the built behaviour with the request, and by then rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the criteria or the plan.
prevention: Require every behaviour criterion to be demonstrated by a test that exercises the real production path end to end, not a default or no-op hook. Here, a landing through the drain must produce a record commit on the records branch. Split multi-part build items into one criterion per part, so the append-only conflict rule has its own demonstration. Add a check before the final verdict that fails when a hook, trait or extension point has only its default implementation, or when the producer's report or the docs say a requested part is undone.
proposed_request: Make the landing queue commit its records after each landing, as described in build job 8 of docs/design/async-drain.md. Outcome: after every landing the drain finishes, the records for that landing are committed by the real drain path, with no default or no-op hook left in place at crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs. Also confirm and enforce the append-only conflict rule for these record commits, and update docs/design/async-drain.md so it no longer says this half is undone. Acceptance: (1) a test runs a real landing through the drain and shows a records commit made after it, at each ordering bound the design lists; (2) a test shows that a record commit conflicting with existing append-only records is refused or resolved as the rule states, and that no existing record is deleted or rewritten; (3) the design doc states both parts as built, with no leftover 'not done' note; (4) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test pass for the workspace, with the commands and output cited in the evidence.
